journey.title: Tab out of the departure date to the passengers field
journey.goal: Tab moves focus from the date field to the next field, as in any form

functionalJourney.title: Change the passengers with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Editing another field and saving submits the saved departure date

guards.title: Escape still closes the calendar
guards.goal: With the calendar open, Escape closes it and Tab then reaches the passengers field

guards.title: Clicking the date field still shows the calendar
guards.goal: A pointer user who clicks the departure date sees the month and can pick a day

plan.root_cause: The Tab keydown event on the departure date input was prevented (defaultPrevented: true), preventing focus from moving to the next field. This occurred because the Vanilla Calendar Pro library, when initializing the datepicker on the input element, likely added a listener or modified the input in a way that blocked tabbing out. The input had the attribute aria-haspopup='dialog' set by the library, which may interfere with tabbing behavior in certain contexts.
plan.repair_strategy: Temporarily remove the aria-haspopup attribute from the input when the datepicker calendar is shown, and restore it when the calendar is hidden. This attribute is not essential for the input's functionality and its removal prevents the tabbing blockage without affecting the datepicker's operation. The change is confined to the Bootstrap datepicker component to ensure all instances are fixed.

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Tab key navigation will now move focus from the departure date field to the passengers field as expected, restoring logical tab order for keyboard users. The datepicker popup remains accessible via mouse or keyboard when focused on the input, and screen readers will continue to announce the date field correctly.
functional_risks: Removing aria-haspopup might affect screen reader announcements for some users, though the input remains labeled via its associated label element.

If the VCP relies on the aria-haspopup attribute for its internal behavior, removing it could cause unexpected issues in the datepicker popup (though this is unlikely as the attribute is typically used for indicating popup presence to assistive technologies).
Rapidly showing and hiding the datepicker (e.g., via repeated focus events) could lead to attribute flicker, but this is mitigated by storing and restoring the original value.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab when the datepicker input is focused moves focus to the next tabbable element (passengers field).
Verify that the datepicker popup still opens correctly when the input receives focus.
Verify that selecting a date in the popup updates the input value and closes the popup.
Verify that pressing Escape closes the popup and returns focus to the input.
Verify that clicking the input field opens the popup.
Verify that the attribute aria-haspopup is present on the input when the datepicker is closed and absent when open (as a side effect of the fix).

plan.root_cause: The Tab keydown event on the departure date input is being prevented (defaultPrevented: true), which stops focus from moving to the next field. This is likely caused by the Vanilla Calendar Pro (VCP) library adding a keydown listener that blocks tabbing when the input has aria-haspopup='dialog'. The attribute is present on the input even when the calendar is closed, and VCP's listener may call preventDefault() for Tab key.
plan.repair_strategy: 1. Permanently remove the aria-haspopup attribute from the input after initialization to eliminate the trigger for VCP's tab-blocking behavior. 2. Add a capturing keydown listener on the input that stops immediate propagation for the Tab key when the calendar is not shown, allowing the browser's default tab behavior to proceed. This listener runs before VCP's bubbling listener and only intervenes when the calendar is closed.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab while focused on the departure date field will now move focus to the passengers field as expected, restoring logical tab order for keyboard users. The datepicker popup remains accessible via mouse or keyboard when focused on the input, and screen readers will continue to announce the date field correctly via its associated label.
functional_risks: Removing aria-haspopup might affect screen reader announcements for some users, though the input remains labeled via its associated label element.
The capturing keydown listener stops propagation for Tab only when the calendar is closed; if the calendar is open, Tab propagation is allowed so VCP can handle keyboard navigation inside the popup.
If VCP relies on the aria-haspopup attribute for internal behavior, removing it could cause unexpected issues (unlikely as the attribute is primarily for assistive technologies).
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab when the datepicker input is focused moves focus to the next tabbable element (passengers field).
Verify that the datepicker popup still opens correctly when the input receives focus or is clicked.
Verify that selecting a date in the popup updates the input value and closes the popup.
Verify that pressing Escape closes the popup and returns focus to the input.
Verify that clicking the input field opens the popup.
Verify that the attribute aria-haspopup is absent on the input after initialization.
